Comments: On July 28, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Papa Bear Well Site in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of fluid reported to the Department on 7/28/2021. The initial report indicated that approximately 40 gallons of production fluid was released from a dump line associated with the Gas Production unit. At the time of inspection, EQT Rep. David Crayne, Jona Stoskey (Moody) and SPSI were on site evaluating the area impacted by the release. The release occurred from the dump line associated with GPU 10H well at a connection on the left side of the GPU. The area impacted by this release was previously impacted by a release of production fluid reported to the Department on 6/25/2021 IR 3212309 which occurred on the right side of the same 10H GPU. According to Ms. Stoskey, she was on site to collect confirmatory sample from the location in accordance with the Act 2 clean up when the release was observed and reported. Mr. Crayne indicated that the most recent spill would also be remediated in accordance with Act 2 and included with the release and clean up form the release on 6/25/2021. New violations area being issued based on the observations made during the site inspection. Violations remain outstanding as indicated on IR 321309.

Comments: At time of inspection: There were twelve wells on site, the Jeffers Farm P2 7H, 8H, 9H, 10H, 11H, 12H, 13H, 14H, 15H, 16H, 17H and 18H. All of the wells were active. There was no gas detected in the vicinity of the well or the GPUs. All gas checks were conducted with a MSA Altair 5X multi gas detector that was calibrated on 4/2/25. I took a walk around the location and there were no obvious concerns noticed. There were no new violations noted.

Comments: On September 21, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3582382 where violations were issued in response to a spill caused by a GPU dumpline failure.The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photos 2 and 3). Some erosion rills were observed in the access road (see photos 4 and 5). Secondary containment was added to the GPU units onsite, and the impacted area was backfilled (see photos 10 and 11). A well tag was present on well 6H, with no observed leaks or discharge on the ground around it, and it appeared to be equipped for production (see photo 13). There are three other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 8). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 12). Seven rolloff dumpsters labeled "production water impacted solids" were onsite (see photos 7 and 9). After inspection was conducted, the Department spoke via phone with EQT representative David Crayne, who stated that remediation was complete and Act 2 is nearly ready for submittal to ECB. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance be conducted on the access road to prevent worsening accelerated erosion and sedimentation onsite. Closure of violations shall be contingent upon Act 2 approval and a subsequent CEI inspection.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8182285
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/04/2024
Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

Comments: On July 10, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of Burnett Oil Co Inc's Stickle Ross Mountain Unit 1H located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following an Oil and Gas Inspector referral during IR 4010435 where the Department observed the following:"There are two areas that appear to have oil staining. The area Southeast of the well is where the pump was during plugging and is approximately 25feet long and extends under the frac tank. The area North of the plugged well has several smaller spots 1-3 feet in diameter, and is where the rig was placed during plugging."Accompanying during today's inspection is Tyler Metzger (WQS DEP).At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance and inside the on-site mailbox was an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Violations for the Act 9 Sign and the ERP are being issued under 129-28411.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Stickle well site to have 2 wells on it. The 1H: 129- 28411 well appears to be in production, while the 1H: 129-28648 appeared to be plugged with a vented monument. A well marker was observed to be leaning up against the wellhead with the well's permit number and a plug date of 7/17/2018, however, according to Department inspection records, this well was reportedly re-plugged on 7/1/2025. The Department is requesting Oil and Gas Inspector follow-up for evaluation of compliance for the well marker. The Department did not observe any active fluid leaks or fluid discharges coming from or near this reportedly re-plugged well. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the two frac tanks, the half round flow back tank and the trailer that were observed during IR 4010435 to be removed from the well site. The 25' long oil stain where the frac tanks were, along with multiple oil stained spots where the rig was sitting were observed on the graveled well pad. The oily substance did not have a sheen but had an unrecognizable odor. The Department screened the oil stained areas with a conductivity meter and collected readings of 0.1422 mS, 0.215 mS, and 0.0019 mS. The Department also observed darker soil around the plugged well, therefore this area was screened as well and a reading of 0.0343 mS was collected. The Department also observed a metallic gold thick substance on the gravel in one of the oil stains, this substance appears to be pipe sealant. The Department recommends the Operator remediate these release(s) in accordance with 78a66(c)(1).The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and a plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is also requesting the Operator clarify what the oily substance(s) is, how the release was quantified and submit the waste manifest from the site remediation upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the oily substance(s) on the graveled well pad.

Permit API: 047-24975
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Jones Township

Inspection Date: 4/21/2026
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Alexis Jacobs, WQS with the Department, on April 20th, 2026. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on the E08-T well pad.It was reported that approximately 1 barrel of production fluid was released from a maintenance failure on a pump used to support the transport of production fluid through a pipeline. The failure was immediately addressed and corrected to stop the production fluid from leaving the pipeline. The pump was in secondary containment, although a majority of the production fluid discharged outside of the containment onto the well pad and onto the fill material beyond the well pad. Upon arrival to the site, a skid steer was being used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. One dumpster was on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. A second dumpster was being transported to the site at the time of this inspection. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred on the well pad. A mini excavator was used to scrape approximately an inch of surface material from the pad where the spill occurred. This material was in a pile to be removed from the pad and placed into a dumpster for disposal. The impacted soils beyond the edge of the well pad were also excavated and placed into a dumpster for disposal. The excavated area beyond the pad was approximately 10 yards x 5 yards. Evidence of production fluid did not appear to be present beyond the excavated area. A copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department when available.Confirmatory field sampling will need to occur to confirm full remediation of the site. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 989361
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident - response to an accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. On 3/18/2023 Chesapeake reported that 10 gallons of produced water sprayed out of a damaged pipe on a GPU unit, the water impacting the unprotected pad surface. Creston Environmental identified the extent of the impacted area and excavation was scheduled for 3/20/2023. It was 39 degrees and clear when I arrived on location.When I first arrived at the site, I met Chesapeake's Pat Adams who described activities with the event. Pat showed me a pipe nipple on the 1HC GPU that had been replaced. He showed me the excavated area that is in the northeast corner of the site. The excavated hole had not been backfilled at the time of the inspection. The excavated area is roughly 12' x 40' with various depths up to 2', running along the edge of the perimeter berm. The GPU had been moved from the affected area and had not been returned back to its original position. Pat said that a truck driver first witnessed the spill. Upon discovery, all ten wells were shut in. Pat had just put the 9 unaffected wells back into production before my arrival. The 1HC was still shut in until the GPU is reinstalled. The excavated material remains on site and has been piled on a plastic sheet on the southeast corner of the pad. I field tested some small water puddles in the bottom of the excavated area with results being as high as 4.18 mS conductance. Using a Hanna Gro-line soil probe, I probed the side of the excavated area with one reading being 1.03 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance of the water and soil with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein. Eric said he would have someone probe the excavated area to determine if further excavation was necessary. Eric also reported that it was their practice not to fill in the excavated area until they had gotten confirmation samples back. Danielle Schaad met me on location before I left and we discussed the elevated conductance areas. She said that they would excavate some more of the area as determined by the results of field tests.There were nine wells staged for production and one offline at the time of the inspection. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. Water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment field tested at 4.55 mS conductance. There are seven frac tanks on site along with one gas buster that were located in secondary containment. Pat reported that the wells were sending their production fluid directly to the production tank. He said the frac tanks were not being used but were still on site in case of inclement weather.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was noted on the east perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3459318 for the spill of brine fluid outside of secondary containment.The DEP recommends the following:1. Screen the area impacted by the release of production fluid for additional contaminants and continue with the excavation as determined by the screening results.2. Remove the water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment at the earliest convenience.I left the site at 1335 hours.

Danielle Schaad met me on location before I left and we discussed the elevated conductance areas. She said that they would excavate some more of the area as determined by the results of field tests.There were nine wells staged for production and one offline at the time of the inspection. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. Water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment field tested at 4.55 mS conductance. There are seven frac tanks on site along with one gas buster that were located in secondary containment. Pat reported that the wells were sending their production fluid directly to the production tank. He said the frac tanks were not being used but were still on site in case of inclement weather.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was noted on the east perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3459318 for the spill of brine fluid outside of secondary containment.The DEP recommends the following:1. Screen the area impacted by the release of production fluid for additional contaminants and continue with the excavation as determined by the screening results.2. Remove the water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment at the earliest convenience.I left the site at 1335 hours.

Later that day, Tony called me back and said that a Rockdale representative would come out to the site to do additional conductivity screening and he would have a vac truck out to suck up the puddle. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Violation ID: 8250188
Permit API: 123-49050
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/29/2025
Comments: I received notification from Oil and Gas Management regarding a public report of water being discharged from the Brown #1 well site, it was stated there was an odd smell, there was concern about if it was safe to be discharged. I arrived onsite and found a hose running down hill from a tank battery on Farm Lane that was used to hold presumed fresh water during the recent completion of this well. The well operator was draining the water tank and using it to water their freshly seeded and mulched areas. I used my conductivity probe and determined the water being discharged from the tank was not suitable to be dispersed to the ground as the conductance of the fluid was in excess of 16000S, which is above the allowable limit of 1000S. The operator immediately shut the valve and ceased the discharge. It is estimated over 1 barrel of fluid was released prior to closing the valve. Mr. Branch called to get additional equipment onsite to begin remediating the release. It was advised to get a vac truck for any standing water, and the mini excavator on site to begin soil removal.From the end of the discharge hose, the water ran approximately 35 feet in a westerly direction across a portion of the site, reaching an open earthen drainage ditch, this ditch connects to the local storm sewer somewhere along Crestview Blvd. Flowing water in the storm sewer was observed at the bottom of Crestview Blvd, due to lack of access I was unable to get my conductivity probe into the water to determine if it was from the Brown #1 site.

Comments: An inspection of the Cummings Lumber 9H well was conducted on November 9, 2023 at 10:50 am. At the time of inspection, the rig is rigging down after plugging operations and the operator is in the process of pouring gravel in the surface section of the wellbore above all plugs. This process was ceased temporarily for the evaluation and inspection of the well at this time. Approximately 3-4% methane and 60% LEL was detected at the top of the well casing with an Altair 5x gas meter at this time. Additionally, approximately 2000 PPM-M was detected with a Remote Methane Leak Detector (RMLD). The operator has reported no pressure or gas detected during recent internal inspections. It was theorized at this time that pouring of gravel may be displacing the static gas in the wellbore, causing it to vacate the wellbore and detectable at surface. It was decided at this time to continue filling the wellbore with gravel and re-inspect. Continued pouring gravel at 11:15 am. They finished pouring gravel at 12:00:pm. The operator plans to cut plugged well below ground level and bury to finalize plugging at this time. Repsol will be submitting a signed Certificate of Well Plugging including an "As Plugged" well-bore schematic with further plugging details.

Permit API: 005-31212

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/10/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going lost water case involving lost water in nearby water well (CTS#373862). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 4 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well bore. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: OGA3215(F) - WELL LOCATION RESTRICTIONS -FLOODPLAINS - Failure to follow requirements for a well site in a floodplain, floodway or flood fringe.
Violation ID: 8249434
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: The purpose of this routine inspection is to document a surface water encroachment resulting from the construction of the Akins Lease Akins #3 OG Well well pad. The well permit for Akins #3 was not observed anywhere onsite at the time of this inspection. Surface permitting biologists Samantha Lutz (DEP) and Jessica McDuff (DEP) were onsite for the duration of the inspection to confirm findings documented in the 08/04/2025 pre-construction inspection (Inspection # 4028638). Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) was also present. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) arrived midway through the inspection.TMP opted to ignore advice given through the 08/04/2025 pre-construction inspection report and an 08/26/2025 field meeting. During the 08/26/2025 field meeting I advised Kyle Miller of the existing surface concerns in the vicinity of the staked well location, and made recommendations for maintaining appropriate setback distances per chapter 105 regulations.At the time of this inspection, it was observed that the well pad was constructed atop an unnamed tributary of Jackson Run pictured in the 08/04/2025 inspection images. The defined bed and banks of this stream are visible above the cut bank of the constructed well pad (Image 4), which suggests that excavation of the stream bed occurred during the construction of this well pad. It was also observed that dirt and gravel fill material was used to build up the site of the well pad atop the stream.A diversion ditch was constructed along the upslope perimeter of the well pad for the conveyance of roadway and well pad runoff, and apparently to accept the flow of the tributary stream that terminates abruptly on the cut bank of the well pad. This diversion ditch is then directed into a culvert on the west edge of the well site (Image 2). The outflow of the culvert appears to return to the defined bed and banks of the unnamed tributary of Jackson Run. Several erosion and sediment control concerns are present in this current configuration.A pit has been excavated on the well pad. Title 25, Chapters 78.61 and 78.62 outline the requirements for the use of a pit as a disposal area for drill cuttings and residual waste generated during the development of a conventional well. These regulations state that a disposal area may not be located within 100 feet of either a stream or wetland. The use of this pit as a disposal area would be in violation of the aforementioned regulations.A notice of violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection for the failure to obtain the appropriate Chapter 105 permit(s) prior to the construction of a water encroachment and for the failure to post the well permit during the construction of the well pad and its access road. In order to achieve compliance with respect to the Chapter 105.11 violation, an application for the appropriate Chapter 105 permit will need to be submitted and ultimately issued. It is requested that TMP produce for the Department surveyed site maps depicting the as-built configuration of all recent construction activities that have occurred on the Akins lease including road improvement/widening of existing lease roads, access road construction, and well pad construction for both the proposed Akins #3 OG well and the un-permitted Akins #4 proposed well.It is requested that TMP produce for the Department a full stream and wetland delineation in the vicinity of construction activities on the Akins lease. It is expected that the findings of such a delineation be documented on site maps depicting each stream, wetland, and drainage feature.It is requested that TMP report the acreage of earth disturbance resulting from the recent construction activities on the Akins lease, including road improvement/widening of existing lease roads.

Violation ID: 839701

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-22
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCDT inspection of the JKLM Sweden Valley 106 Well Pad located in Sweden Twp, Potter Co. on 1/22/2019 @1130 hours. The weather was 16 degrees, overcast, winds S@9mph. Approximately 12" of snow was deposited onsite in the previous 72 hours. JKLM representative Scott West and DEP Env Trainee, Korey Starkey was present onsite. JKLM contractor Pro Frac is currently stimulating the 6 utica wells onsite. Mr. West stated at the time of this inspection they had just completed stimulating stage 13 of the 2HU well, and perforating stage 7 of the 5HU well. Two small spills have been reported within the last week on the SV 106 well site, during the frack. Spill #1 (CTS#339324), occurred and was reported on 1/16/2019. The spill reportedly involved the release of 400 to 500 gallons of brine from the working tank. The spill was reportedly mostly on primary containment with some spray hitting the perimeter of the pad. As of today's inspection the secondary containment around the working tanks was full of snow. One area in the containment, which appeared to be a high foot traffic area, had slush/fluid mix with a field measure conductivity of "Over Range". A vac truck was dispatched to remove the fluid. The containment had recently been repaired in the same area. No melted slush or fluid was observed outside of containment. Additional screening, when conditions allow, under and around the secondary containment was discussed with a representative from Whipper Hill Consulting while onsite. Spill #2 (CTS#339357), occurred and was reported on 1/18/2019. This spill involved the reported release of a few hundred gallons of produced water into containment from a pump filter. The containment berm was compressed allowing 20-30 gallons of produced water to leave the containment impacting the pad surface. As of today's inspection the area along the perimeter of the compromised containment where the spill occurred was snow covered. No melted or stained areas were observed. An onsite representative from Whipper Hill Consulting provided grid drawings of pre and post excavation soil conductivity readings of the impacted area. The highest recorded soil conductivity reading was 1.44mS/cm, the remaining readings were <1.0mS/cm. Excavated materials were placed in waste containers and staged inside containment awaiting disposal. Violations of 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(B) and SWMA 301 are cited as Immediate Corrected at this time. Please address any deficiencies noted and contact me with any questions. I departed the site at 1300 hours. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 369324
